finding.claim: wipe() ignores the boolean returned by requireRole(), so the OWNER check is never enforced. Any caller can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: POST /tenants/{t}/wipe: the caller's User (any role, even an empty role set) and the tenant path parameter
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, which destroys the tenant's data

trace.note: requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) and never throws, as its Javadoc says
wipe() calls requireRole(u, "OWNER") and discards the result

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is the ignored requireRole call. checkRole, which throws, is used in export() but not here. No other auth middleware is visible in the repo, because Admin.java is the only file. The tenant is not compared to the caller's tenant.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole(u, "OWNER") at src/Admin.java:26 — returns boolean, never throws, result discarded; no other guard (checkRole at :18 throws but is only used in export() at :32; Admin.java is the only file).
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls the non-throwing boolean requireRole (defined at :14-16) as a bare statement, so repo.wipe(tenant) at :27 runs for any authenticated caller regardless of role, unlike export() which uses the throwing checkRole at :32.

finding.claim: Roles are a global set of strings and are not scoped to a tenant. wipe() and export() never check that the caller owns the tenant named in the URL, so an OWNER of any tenant can act on another tenant (cross-tenant authorization failure).
finding.source: The tenant path parameter in POST /tenants/{t}/export (and /wipe), with a caller whose roles contain "OWNER" for some other tenant
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33, and repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27

trace.note: User holds only name and a flat Set<String> roles, with no tenant binding
checkRole tests only role membership and takes no tenant argument
checkRole(u, "OWNER") passes for an owner of any tenant
repo.export is called with the unvalidated tenant from the URL

finding.guards_checked: No tenant-membership or ownership comparison is visible in this file. The check could exist in a layer that is not in the repo (such as the Repo implementation or a middleware), so this is a precondition-dependent finding.

verdict.guard_found: Only checkRole(u,"OWNER") at src/Admin.java:32 (throws, but tests a global role with no tenant argument). In wipe(), requireRole at :26 returns a boolean that is discarded, so it gives no protection at all. No other source files exist (src/Admin.java is the only file), so no tenant-scoping layer is visible.
verdict.reason: Every traced line matches. User has a flat Set<String> roles (Admin.java:4), checkRole takes no tenant (:18-22), and export() passes the URL tenant straight to repo.export (:32-33). The attacker is an authenticated OWNER of some other tenant, so they do not already hold power over the target tenant. wipe() is worse than claimed: the result of requireRole is discarded at :26, so any authenticated user can reach repo.wipe at :27. The only caveat is that a tenant check could exist in the unseen Repo implementation or in middleware.
